---
title: Vault & MCP Credentials
description: How OMA isolates upstream credentials from the agent and the sandbox using a main-side credential proxy.
---

OMA's vault is the single source of truth for upstream credentials (MCP-server tokens, OAuth tokens, API keys). The agent itself — whether the cloud DO running `generateText`, the local daemon spawning `claude-agent-acp`, or the sandbox container running `curl` — **never holds plaintext credentials in memory**. All three callers know only `(tenantId, sessionId, server-name | hostname)` and ask the **main worker** to make the actual upstream call on their behalf. Main looks up the credential **live on every call**, injects the bearer, and forwards.

Mirrors the [Claude Managed Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents) "credential proxy outside the harness" pattern: a prompt-injected agent has no credential to leak because there is none in its address space.

## Three callers, one resolver

```text
                    ┌──────────────────┐
                    │  Vault (D1+KV)   │  single source of truth
                    └────────┬─────────┘
                             │ live read on EVERY call
              ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
              │  apps/main worker            │
              │  resolveProxyTargetByTenant  │  URL match
              │  resolveOutboundCredentialByHost  │  hostname match
              │  forwardWithRefresh          │  inject + 401-refresh
              └──┬─────────┬───────────┬────┘
                 │         │           │
        ┌────────┘         │           └────────┐
        │ HTTP             │ RPC                │ RPC
        ▼                  ▼                    ▼
  ACP child          Cloud agent DO         Sandbox container
  (laptop daemon)    (in-Worker)            (HTTPS interceptor)
        │                  │                    │
        └─ NONE of these three holds plaintext credentials ─┘
```

| Caller | Knows | Asks |
|---|---|---|
| Local-runtime ACP child | `(sid, server, agent api key)` | HTTP `/v1/oma/mcp-proxy/<sid>/<server>` with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` |
| Cloud agent DO | `(tenantId, sid, server)` | `env.MAIN_MCP.mcpForward(...)` via service-binding RPC (binding scope = auth) |
| Sandbox container | full upstream URL | `env.MAIN_MCP.outboundForward(...)` via the agent worker's outbound interceptor |

For host-bound credentials of every kind, the wire field `mcp_server_url` is a compatibility name: it identifies the target host for credential matching, including ordinary API and git hosts, not just MCP servers.

## Handles: several credentials for one host

On self-host `oma-vault`, a **handle** lets a sandbox select a bearer or CLI
credential when several credentials match the same host. Set `auth.handle` on
the credential to the HTTP Basic username the sandbox sends. For example, a
git remote can use:

```text
https://<handle>:placeholder@github.com/org/repo.git
```

Replace `<handle>` with the exact value configured by your sandbox image or
environment, and copy that same value into the credential's **Handle** field.
The sandbox configuration chooses and sends this username; the vault does not
choose it or configure the sandbox for you. The password is a placeholder:
`oma-vault` selects the matching credential and replaces the outgoing
Authorization header with the real authentication. For git smart-HTTP requests,
it injects Basic auth with the stored token as the password.

A handle is optional when only one credential matches the host. For selection
when credentials share a host, see the existing
[credential precedence rules](/reference/configuration/#http-basic-credentials).

## HTTP Basic (self-host)

Use `static_basic` for username/password APIs such as Langfuse. Store the public
key as `username` and secret key as `token`; `oma-vault` injects Basic auth on REST
and OTLP paths and replaces sandbox placeholders. Passwords are omitted from API
responses and can be rotated without restarting the session. Basic credentials
never trigger OAuth refresh. See the [Langfuse setup](/self-host/node-docker/#langfuse-with-http-basic)
and [credential reference](/reference/configuration/#http-basic-credentials).

## Google Drive and Docs with a service account

1. In your Google Cloud project, enable the **Google Drive API** and **Google
   Docs API**, then create a service account. Create and download a JSON key
   from its **Keys** tab. See [Google's service-account setup](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/service-account).
2. Add the key's `client_email` to the target **shared drive** as **Content
   manager**. A service account has no Drive storage of its own (quota **0**).
   The bot must create files inside that shared drive or a folder inside it.
   Creating files elsewhere, including an ordinary shared My Drive folder,
   fails with a `storageQuotaExceeded` quota error. Sharing an existing My
   Drive folder as Editor only allows work on existing files.
   See [shared drives](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/about-shareddrives)
   and [permission roles](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/ref-roles).
3. From your operator machine, create the vault credential. Keep the downloaded
   key on that machine; do not copy it into the sandbox. The API accepts the
   full Google JSON object or its JSON string in `key_json`:

```python
import json
import os
import urllib.request

with open("service-account.json") as key_file:
    key = json.load(key_file)
payload = {
    "display_name": "Research Bot Google",
    "auth": {
        "type": "service_account_jwt",
        "mcp_server_url": "https://www.googleapis.com/",
        "key_json": key,
        "scopes": "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents",
    },
}
request = urllib.request.Request(
    os.environ["BASE"] + "/v1/vaults/" + os.environ["VAULT_ID"] + "/credentials",
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "x-api-key": os.environ["KEY"]},
    method="POST",
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
    credential = json.load(response)  # Response omits the private key.
```

4. Attach the vault to the session's `vault_ids`. In a sandbox routed through
   self-host `oma-vault`, call Drive with any placeholder bearer:

```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer placeholder' \
  'https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files?supportsAllDrives=true&includeItemsFromAllDrives=true'
```

The [Docs REST API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/docs/api/reference/rest/v1/documents/get)
uses `docs.googleapis.com`. Create a second credential with the same key and
scopes but `mcp_server_url: "https://docs.googleapis.com/"` for that host:

```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer placeholder' \
  'https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/DOCUMENT_ID'
```

Leave `subject` unset for access through direct sharing. For domain-wide
delegation, a Workspace administrator must authorize the service account's
client ID and scopes first; then set `subject` to the user being impersonated.
Scopes alone do not grant access to unshared files.

The vault signs a one-hour JWT (`iss`, `scope`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`, optional
`sub` and header `kid`), exchanges it at the HTTPS `token_uri`, and injects the
returned access token. It renews within five minutes of expiry and retries
once after an upstream 401. Key material, assertions and tokens stay outside
the sandbox. Minted tokens are encrypted in the credential store with a
revision check; an in-process cache and single-flight prevent duplicate mints
within that process. Separate processes may mint concurrently.

Rotate from the credential's console detail or update `auth.key_json` through
the API. Metadata edits such as scopes, subject or host invalidate old cached
tokens. List/get never return the private key or token. Cloudflare forwarding
rejects this kind explicitly. A same-host `static_bearer` has equal rank and
the first match wins; use unambiguous host bindings. See the
[credential reference](/reference/configuration/#service-account-jwt-credentials).

## OAuth refresh

For credentials of type `mcp_oauth`, the proxy automatically handles 401:

1. Upstream returns 401
2. Re-fetch the credential row from D1 — if `access_token` already moved past the stale one (a concurrent call refreshed first), use the live token. Otherwise:
3. POST `token_endpoint` with the `refresh_token`
4. Persist rotated `{access_token, refresh_token, expires_at}` back to D1 via `services.credentials.refreshAuth`
5. Retry once with the new bearer

If refresh itself fails (revoked refresh_token, scope change), the second upstream call returns the original 401 to the caller. No false-success masking.

## What the model sees

Tools registered as `mcp__<server>__<tool_name>` with full schemas — first-class AI SDK tools, not stringly-typed wrappers. The model picks tools by name + structured arguments; the platform handles auth and forwarding.

```text
agent.mcp_tool_use:
  name: mcp__linear__list_issues
  input: { team: "OpenMA", limit: 1, orderBy: "updatedAt" }

agent.mcp_tool_result:
  content: { issues: [{ id: "OPE-48", title: "...", status: "Done", ... }] }
```

The model never sees the bearer token — only the response.

## Audit trail

Every call through `forwardWithRefresh` emits a structured log line:

```json
{
  "op": "mcp_proxy.forward",
  "caller": "http" | "rpc-mcp" | "rpc-outbound",
  "tenant_id": "...",
  "session_id": "...",
  "server": "linear",
  "host": "mcp.linear.app",
  "method": "POST",
  "status": 200,
  "refreshed": true | false,
  "ms": 1234
}
```

Production incident response can answer "who called what when" without per-call-site instrumentation.

## Limits

- **`command_secret` credentials** (e.g. `GIT_TOKEN` injected as env var on `git` commands) flow into the sandbox container's per-command process env. AST-gated to single-simple-command form (composite `&&`/`;`/`|` blocks injection) — casual `env | grep` from the model returns nothing. **Targeted prompt injection** that crafts single-command-form leak vectors specific to the binary can still exfiltrate. Don't attach high-blast-radius credentials (org-wide GitHub PAT, prod database creds) to agents handling untrusted input until command_secret moves to the same out-of-sandbox proxy pattern as MCP/outbound.

- **Streaming uploads** through `outboundForward` — current RPC body type is `string | null`. Multi-MB binary uploads from `curl -F file=@big.pdf` would need the body type widened first.

- **Rate limiting** — no per-credential / per-session quota in mcp-proxy yet. A misbehaving agent can spam an upstream until it rate-limits the entire tenant.
